note: ** The `holdings_watchlist` depth scanned exactly 10 names, and two of the twelve focus names — GS and KKR — arrived as tape/8-K promotions with *no scan row at all*: no ATR, no RSI, no trend labels, no chart, no anchored VWAP. GS carries the second-strongest 30-day EPS revisions in the entire universe screen (+18.75%) and `institutions_buying_price_weak`, and I had to shelve it purely because I could not place an honest stop or judge entry geometry. This is the same defect logged as LP-8200625986 on 2026-07-19 for MU, still unfixed: **tape/8-K promotions should inherit the full scan row (ATR, trend, volume signal, anchored VWAP) and a chart, not just news and fundamentals** — otherwise the promotion mechanism surfaces names it cannot let me underwrite, which is worse than not surfacing them. Second, smaller: my own CRWD trigger was conditioned on a confirmed MACD bull cross, an indicator this system's own 12-year study measured at −0.01pp. Nothing flagged the contradiction between a stored watchlist trigger and a knowledge-base finding that retired the indicator — a cheap check comparing trigger text against measured-dead indicators would have caught it a week ago.

** the watchlist trigger checker is **direction-blind**, and that is what produced this run's false positive. My published PANW condition was a *reclaim* of ~$345 that *holds*; the alert fired because price came within 2% of $345 **from below** (live $340.12, -2.45% on the day) — the opposite of the stated condition. This is the same class of defect as LP-4566902391 (the AMD alert firing 3.9% off the level). Fix: parse a relation token out of `would_buy_at` — "reclaim / above / breaks out / closes above" requires price **at or above** the level, "pullback to / near / dip to / below" requires price **at or below** — and only fire when the relation is satisfied, defaulting to proximity-only with an explicit `relation: unknown` tag when no token parses. Secondary, same block: the alert quoted PANW's stale 7/20 close ($348.66) while `live_prices.json`, written four minutes earlier, carried $340.12 — the alert rows should quote the same live mark the `trigger_run_note` claims to have confirmed on, or the two blocks will keep contradicting each other on exactly the days a trigger matters.

** The three ideas that actually competed for capital this run — UNH, TRV and MPC — are all *non-focus* names, so the bundle gave me a numeric scan row and nothing else: no candlestick chart, no options-implied expected move, no `stop_engineering` floor, no `ownership_flow`, no insider read. I had to judge UNH's entry geometry against a 200-week moving average I could not see on a chart, and I have no idea whether its options market is leaning the way GS's is. This is adopted lesson LP-8200625986 recurring verbatim, and today it was the *deciding* constraint rather than a nuisance: the scanner should promote the top 2–3 non-focus `top_setups` rows (or any name carrying a >5% 30-day upward EPS revision) into the focus set each run so they receive a chart plus the deep bundle. As it stands, the moment leadership rotates out of my 13 focus names — which is precisely what a momentum unwind *is* — my research depth rotates out with it.
